findings.title: The new downsize definition replaces the existing API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods, so this definition replaces the four-dimension-argument `downsize` method immediately above it. Existing calls such as `downsize(from, to, width, height)` now treat `height` as the options argument and fail while building resize instructions; calls that also pass options raise an argument error. Preserve both call forms in one method or update every caller.

findings.title: Oversized animated GIFs can be permanently reduced to one frame
findings.body: When an oversized GIF is uploaded while `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, this call selects the non-animated downsize path. That path reads only the GIF's first frame, and the result is written back to the upload's original tempfile, so the stored upload becomes a still image and the remaining animation frames are lost. Thumbnail animation settings should not silently destroy animation in the original upload.

findings.title: Upload validation no longer honors the attachment size setting
findings.body: This applies a fixed 10 MB limit to both images and attachments, even though validation receives the upload type and previously used the corresponding site setting. Sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB now block valid files in the browser; sites with a lower attachment limit let oversized files through to a server-side rejection instead of enforcing the configured limit here.
